utterances.text: Can you tell me how come that you know them? From where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: Well, it's all the people from the neighbourhood, from that part of the town. And we mostly knew each other and indeed we still do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you say that this is what happened. Could you be more specific. Did they come? Did Vinko come? How did they can came? Did they contact you or maybe the other Muslim families? How did it happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: Well, Vinko did come, every now and again, quite frequently. We would speak to him. He would ask whether we had any problems, did anyone come and bother us or mistreat us? But mostly nothing happened. So we felt no need to call him. But he would come on his own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, throughout this period, did anyone come to your door again, either from the army, the soldiers, or did anyone come to bother you at all again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: Well, yes. There was looting going on in the part of the town in a certain period of time. People would come into the -- break into the apartments and take all the valuables and one evening they came to our apartment. I opened the door. My parents were there. And my younger sister was also there. There were three men in uniform. I didn't see their insignia. They said that they had come, that they were from Stela's unit. I didn't know them. But I didn't dare to say anything. What could I say? They entered the apartment. Asked for our documents, and one of them got ready to take away the TV and some other valuables. He asked if there was anybody else living in the apartment? And I said, yes, my older sister. I didn't call her. I showed her ID because she was in the HVO at the beginning of the war with the Serbs and that's how she retained this ID card. When they saw it, they left, like there is nothing we can do here. There is nothing that -- nothing for us here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You did mention that there was looting going on in that part of the town, and that the men that came wanted to take away your TV set and so on. Let's take it one thing at a time. What kind of looting? Who did it? What did you see? Could you please clarify this a bit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: As to what I saw or heard, they entered the apartments below me. They did it so quietly that nobody realised it. Nobody else realised it and they took away all the valuables.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear how many were they, what kinds of people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: Well, usually it would be two or three men in uniforms and they would claim that they were members of Stela's unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the same manner in which the three men that came to your apartment operated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How can we then understand it? How do you know that this man wanted to take away your TV set? What did he do to make you think that he wanted to take your TV set?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: Well, while we were standing out in the corridor talking to him, he entered my room. He unplugged the TV set and he rolled up the wire and the -- also did the same thing with the video. And he set it all up so that he can take it away when he left. The same thing happened in the other room. They were asking for -- looking for gold, money, valuables.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So when they finally when they saw this ID card they left without taking anything with them. Could you please tell me, did you notify anyone about this event? More specifically I want to know whether you notified Vinko Martinovic, Stela, because these men had purported to be members of Stela's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: This happened in the evening. Right in the morning I went to Vinko and I told him that some men had come claiming that they were from his unit, and he got really angry, and in his anger, he said, "Now we will go from unit to unit, and you will have to identify these men," because he had already heard the rumours about the looting being carried out in such a way in his name. And I told him, "Come on, don't do it. I don't want to cause any more trouble. Because you would just cause problems for yourself. And what happened happened. Let bygones be bygones".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me was it ever determined who these men were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: Yes. I ended up in the police. They came to see me from the criminal investigations division. Since these men, this group of men that looted the apartment, claiming to the Stela's men, Stelici, they were discovered and I was called to come to the police, not to give a statement but to identify, to try and identify some of these people from photographs. I managed to identify two or three of them but wasn't able to identify all of them and then Franjo, who was in the criminal investigations division, told us that one and the same group perpetrated everything that was it going on in our part of the town. They didn't just loot things from Muslims but from Croats too. They were captured on one of these occasions and this is how it all came out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he perhaps tell you the names of these people, the people who were arrested?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: Well, I guess they were their nicknames. One much them was called Slovenac and the other one was called Fadil.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if they were Stela's soldiers? Had this been established?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: No. They were not Stela's soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. Please tell us, you said that you went to see Stela and so on. So do you know where Stela was? What unit he was? Where did you go to see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: Well, it was in Kalemova Street. This is where their base was so to speak. That's where the lads were. I knew that I could always find him there if I needed him for anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, in the period after that, did anything happen, anything of note? Or was it the same as before? In other words did Stela and his soldiers continue coming there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: Yes. They continued coming there. We kept in constant contact. There were no problems, and even if there had been any problems, I knew that Stela would try to help me as much as he could.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Stela persecute any Muslims or anything? Did you see anything like that in your part of the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: No never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear any rumours that he persecuted Muslims, himself or his soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear any rumours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And around town, was there any talk that Stela or Stelici were persecuting Muslims? Did you have hear such stories?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or from some other Muslim neighbours, did you hear that he'd helped them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: Why of course, of course, and praising him and all will praise him always because in that neighbourhood, he was the one who protected it, to all intensive purposes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how he protected? Did he protects by virtue of some powers that he had or in some other way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: Well, because he was brave, because everybody was afraid of him, he was brave and he would have resisted if -- I'm sure if the situation arose, he would have resisted. He wanted to help us and everybody feared him. So that there were no problems at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you personally think that he helped you and your family and offered you some security?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Cross-examination, Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I may use one exhibit depending on the answers of the witness, so if it could be distributed. Cross-examined by Mr. Bos:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. Witness, you've it testified that you were friends with Vinko Martinovic. How close friends were you? You said that he would sometimes take you to school. Would you sometimes visit his house or would he visit sometimes your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: I said we met. I said that we had met, that that was how we met. We knew one another before. But we struck a closer friendship. Yes, he would give me a lift to the school, we'd talk and yes, he would visit me at home, have a coffee, talk, you know, the way one strikes friendships with whoever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were your parents also friends with the Martinovic family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said that you knew Stela's unit and the members of this unit. Do you know what the name of this unit was where Vinko Martinovic was a member of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: Mrmak, yeah, I know it was called Mrmak, Vinko Skrobo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know what Vinko's function was within the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: Well, he was something like a commander of those men of his. He led that unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've said that you knew many of the other soldiers of his unit as well. Could you give me the names of the persons you knew as well, from this unit? First of all, let me ask you, how many people you think did this unit contain? How many members?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you know all 40 or 50 of them or just some of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: I knew some of them. I knew the names of some of them, because they were from my street. But mostly I knew their faces and any way, I remember faces, I don't remember names. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you say that you would remember faces, is that because you very often visited the units and would you see these soldiers at the unit in Kalemova Street, at the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: What do you mean, "Often visited"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you said that you knew some of the soldiers by name and others by face. So my question is when would you see these other members, when you recognised them by face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: I see. Why, we all came from the same neighbourhood, and on the map, it looks very large but it's not large. It's very small. So that we all come across one another all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Witness, let's move to this incident where these three men entered your apartment. Could you give me the -- do you recall the date when this was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: No. I do not remember the exact date. It was in 1993. No, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to clarify something. You've said that these -- there were three men who entered your apartment. And they -- well, and then they took the television or they lined up the television and then when you showed the HVO cards, they left again, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct that these same three men then came back on other occasions to go into other apartments or was it all on the same day and were these the same three men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: Well, that same day, they went to two other apartments in a building next to me and in a flat beneath my apartment. They spent 45 minutes there and they took everything valuable they could find there, from that flat. And after that, they came to our place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they all did this on one day, and they didn't come back any other day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: They did come back to our neighbourhood, to our locality, not to those three buildings that we lived in but they came to other buildings, residential buildings, in that locality and some Muslim houses, standing on their own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that? Did you see that yourself or did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: The gentleman, when I went to the CID department in the police, it was the gentleman, the gentleman who was in charge of that case, and who had asked me to come to the police, he told me that. It was a group of people, uniformed, God only knows who they belonged to, whose only objective was to steal, and that group was caught, once when they tried to rob a petrol pump belonging to a Croat. It was then that they were caught and then the police put two and two together, when it came to incidents of that nature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've testified that you knew two -- you mentioned two names of this group of people who were later caught by the police. And you said that they were not members of Stela's unit. Now, who told you that they were not members of Stela's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: Why, I knew they were not members of Stela's unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're saying because you knew all the members of Stela's unit, you knew that these two people were not members of Stela's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you mentioned these two names, which you identified at the police station, and so you're saying that these two persons were not members of Stela's unit because you knew that they were not members of Stela's unit or did somebody else tell you this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: Now how shall I -- I knew because those two blokes who had those names, they were around town, they were moving about the town, you could hear stories, Slovenac this, Slovenac that, and those were the names that stuck, and I never thought that they were thieves until this thing happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this group of people, this was only three men? Or was the group bigger, that was caught by the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: It was a larger group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how many people were caught by the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: I can't remember. I was shown photographs in the police but they were photographs of people whom I did not know so I cannot remember how many of them there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, why do you think that these people would use the name of Stela's unit when they came into our apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know why. Perhaps to wash their hands, not to -- and perhaps not to be caught, as they were caught then.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit P556, please? I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Bos, could I ask to you ask the witness a question at this stage. Could this witness recall in any way when it was that she was called into the police station to identify the photographs and was told that the group had been arrested?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you hear the question by the Judge? Do you recall when you went to the police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: Perhaps, I'm not sure, it could have been, perhaps, some ten or 15 days after they had broken in, into my apartment. After they had broken in, perhaps ten or 15 days, I cannot -- I really cannot remember exactly. And it was then that the whole group was caught.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Bos, could you follow up with the obvious question?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I did try to ask that question but maybe I can ask --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you try to remember when these people broke into your apartment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought Mr. Bos would start with the documents. I wanted to object before, if it's not yet the turn for the document, then I will wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Give me one second.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Witness, could you again try to remember? Because I asked you before and you had difficulties remembering the date, but could you try to remember when it was that these people broke into your apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: I can't. I can't. I can't remember when exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me help you. Was it after the 9th of May, when the conflict broke out in Mostar, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: Yes, yes, after the 9th of May. After it. It was during the conflict between the Muslims and the Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it a few weeks, a few months, after that event or ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: It could have been a few months later, after the 9th of May. It was 1993. I can't remember when exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I hope this will satisfy the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll come to my exhibit now so I don't know if Mr. Par has any objections?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Par, if you want to make some objections to the using of this document, my advice is wait until it is used. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you get a chance of reading this document? And if you didn't, please read the document, please. Have you read it? The other -- the rest is an English translation so you don't have to read any of the other pages. Now, Witness, this is a report of the military police on the centre of Mostar dated August the 3rd, and it reports about the fact that a large share of the crimes committed in Mostar -- well, that the Vinko Skrobo ATG and the Benko Penavic ATG are responsible for a large share of the crimes committed in the Mostar town. My question is: Could it perhaps be the case that these men who entered your apartment, that they used the name of this unit because it was widely known in West Mostar that the Vinko Skrobo unit committed such crimes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'll move on to another topic. Witness, you lived during the whole year of 1993 in West Mostar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any Muslim friends who were evicted from their houses in West Mostar during that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MD
utterances.text: No. They all stayed. Only my grandmother was expelled. And from the lower part of my neighbourhood people were expelled on the 9th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you say the lower part of your neighbourhood, would that still

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: During the examination, I think the same map used once by the Defence team, the other by the Prosecution, so the D2/30, as well as P11.18/16 are admitted into evidence under seal. Mr. Par, I think you have something to say about the documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I just wanted to tender this map into evidence, if the Prosecution agrees to it, it may be admitted as a Defence Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Yes, it doesn't need to have a Prosecution exhibit number. It can remain D2/30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: The document which I used for this witness has already been admitted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Judge Clark told me that we should trust Mr. Seric's optimism about the proceedings, and I have to offer my congratulations on you because we finished the fifth witness this week, which is a great surprise to me. Anyway, I wish you all a happy weekend and we will meet next Monday, in the afternoon, in Courtroom I. We will rise.
